summary: This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to provide a tax credit for individuals who pay for flood insurance on their primary residence, with different credit limits and phase-out thresholds for federal, private, and contents coverage.

scores.thoughts: This bill introduces a new tax credit, which reduces government revenue and can be considered a form of indirect government spending through tax expenditures. The credit is capped and phased out based on income, but it still represents a cost to the government.

The core of this bill is the creation of a new tax credit for flood insurance expenses, which directly reduces the tax liability for eligible taxpayers. This constitutes a reduction in taxes for those who qualify.

By introducing a new tax credit, this bill would reduce government revenue, which, if not offset by spending cuts, would contribute to an increase in the national debt. The bill does not include any provisions for offsetting this revenue loss.
